messages:
emma: Kicking off polaris-ptq (int4 PTQ) onboarding. Canary run shows structured funcall parse failures ~2.7% vs 0.3% on float baseline. posting a couple raw samples we hit.

emma: sample malformed output (copied from logs):
```
{"action": "charge_card", "args": {"amount": 49.99, "currency": "USD"}}
NOTE: user asked for promo code handling
```

raj: Hmm, trailing `NOTE:` appended by system prompt? that suffix will definitely break strict JSON parse. any pattern on which prompts see it?

sophia: Saw this only on polaris-ptq with longer KV-prefixes; could be kv-cache truncation + model trying to append a human-friendly comment. probably a decoding artifact after EOS handling.

liam: quick heuristic I tried locally: extract the first balanced JSON object with a small regex then parse. reduced parse errors to ~0.6% on the same sample set. not ideal but low-effort. snippet: `re.search(r"\{.*?\}", text, flags=re.DOTALL)`

emma: thanks, liam. Important note: when we add retries, we see duplicate side-effects if the function is non-idempotent (e.g., charge flow). retry-budget helped reduce flapping but made duplicates visible.

sophia: for funcalls we need two things: 1) sanitize to get a clean JSON (heuristic) and 2) avoid blind retries for non-idempotent actions. suggest adding an `idempotency` flag to the tool manifest and only retry safe ones.

raj: Agree. Also suspect batch size / continuous-batching influences suffix noise. polaris-ptq seems to hallucinate a short explanatory suffix when sequences cross a buffer boundary. can we test with batch size 1?

liam: ran a quick A/B: batch=1 -> parse errs 1.5%, batch=8 -> 2.7%. So batching correlates. lowering batch helps but hurts throughput.

emma: Proposed mitigation plan: 
- add a conservative JSON-sanitizer postprocess (heuristic first, then strict fallback)
- tag tools with `idempotent: true|false` and gate automatic retry budget
- reduce default batch for polaris-ptq in canary to 2 (tradeoff throughput vs correctness)
- run 100k synthetic single-tool-call evals to measure regression and dup side-effects

raj: I'll take the sanitizer PR and add structured telemetry (raw output, cleaned output, sanitizer action). Want to log sanitized_count and sanitizer_type.

sophia: I'll own the eval harness run and verify idempotency metrics (duplicate-charge checks, phantom calls).

liam: I'll update canary config: set batch=2, mirror 10% traffic to polaris-ptq, add rollout rule that auto-rolls back if sanitized_count > 0.5% AND duplicate_tool_invokes > 0.02%.

devx: Heads-up — can we get a short doc blurb for DevX to add to onboarding guides about `idempotent` tool metadata and sanitizer? simple example and recommended defaults.

emma: yes, i'll draft. Also CCing ops-bot to schedule the canary.

ops-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: polaris-ptq canary -> 2026-02-03T14:00:00Z (run window 4h).

emma: Thanks all. Follow-ups: raj PR for sanitizer, liam config change, sophia eval run. Let's reconvene after 100k evals or ~4h after canary start.

liam: PR link: https://git.internal/r/polaris/sanitizer (draft) :eyes:

sophia: kicked off eval job `eval/polaris/funcall-100k-20260203` — ETA ~2h. will paste results in thread.

raj: started sanitizer branch, adding verbose logs and a flag `--sanitize-mode=heuristic|strict|off`. default is `heuristic`.

emma: Great. One more ask: add small synthetic tests that intentionally append non-json suffixes (e.g., `\nNote: ...`) to catch regressions in CI.

sophia: Will add to harness.

emma: okay locking this as action items. thx everyone. :party_parrot:
